transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… things have been happening for months now. My sister’s appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people say they forgot to call me back.

Everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes, but it’s too much of a pattern. I think people are keeping information from me, trying to push me out of decisions.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t seen anything like that. I mean, people say things and then deny it, but not voices when no one’s there.
Have you generally been a very distrustful or suspicious person since you were young, or is this level of suspicion something new that started a few months ago?
I wouldn’t say I was always like this. It’s more… it started maybe 11 months ago, when my sister’s health got worse and I had to start handling more of her care. Then I started noticing things.
In the months before this started, did you have any new medical problems, head injury, or changes in substances (alcohol, drugs, or new medications)?

Not that I can think of. I mean… nothing major. I didn’t hit my head or anything like that. I don’t really use drugs, and I don’t think there was some big medication change. It was more just… everything with my sister started piling up.
Over these past several months, have you noticed any changes in your energy, motivation, or interest in things you used to enjoy, or has your ability to function at work or in daily life changed?

I’m still getting things done, mostly. Work, home, all of that. But… I guess people have noticed I’m a little more intense.

Family meetings have gotten tense, and at work I’ve had a few awkward conversations when I pushed harder about mistakes than I probably used to. I’m managing, but it’s… affecting how people react to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a persistent (11-month) fixed delusional belief that others are withholding information and conspiring against her, without hallucinations, disorganized speech, or significant negative symptoms. Functioning is largely preserved aside from relational friction caused by the suspicion, distinguishing this from schizophrenia. Onset correlates with psychosocial stress (sister's declining health/caregiving burden) but no primary medical, substance, or neurological cause was identified, arguing against a secondary psychotic disorder. The circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion in the absence of mood episode or broader psychotic symptomatology is most consistent with Delusional Disorder.
